correctness.rationale: For n>=3, N(a_i)={b_j:j!=i}, N_2(a_i)={a_j:j!=i}, and reciprocally for b_i; matching opposites a_i,b_i are at distance 3. Thus every vertex satisfies precisely the two stated I,J alternatives. If |S|>=4, either both sides contain >=2 vertices or a side has >=3, ensuring the criterion; sets of size <=2 fail. Valid size-3 sets are the two one-sided 3-subsets or mixed 2+1 subsets with unmatched singleton index. Their total is 2*C(n,3)+2*n*C(n-1,2)=4*n*(n-1)*(n-2)/3. Every larger subset contributes C(2n,k), proving the entire enumerator and minimum 3. Independently implemented all vertex-distance cases and subsets n=3..6; the finite checks are corroborative, while the partition proof handles every n>=3.
residual_risks: All-n assertions established from analytic structural argument, not finite experiments.
